messages.content:
Work out the ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category for the episode below. The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed.

Think in three steps: first name the condition chiefly responsible for the admission, second name the ICD-10-AM chapter letter it belongs to, third give the three-character category.

Example 1
Hospital course: A 72-year-old man with a 50 pack-year smoking history was admitted with three days of worsening breathlessness and purulent sputum. Spirometry showed an FEV1/FVC ratio of 0.52. He was treated with nebulised bronchodilators, oral prednisolone and antibiotics for an infective exacerbation of his long-standing airflow limitation.
Answer: Irreversible airflow limitation in a heavy smoker with an infective exacerbation is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, chapter J, category J44.
CODE: J44

Example 2
Hospital course: A 58-year-old man presented with crushing central chest pain radiating to the jaw. The electrocardiogram showed ST elevation in the anterior leads and high-sensitivity troponin rose from 40 to 2100 ng/L. He underwent primary percutaneous coronary intervention with a stent to the proximal left anterior descending artery.
Answer: ST elevation with a rising troponin and culprit-vessel stenting is an acute myocardial infarction, chapter I, category I21.
CODE: I21

Hospital course:
Discharge Summary:

Admission Date: [Date]
Discharge Date: [Date]

Patient Name: [Name]
Sex: [Gender]
Age: 70 years old
Primary Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Hospital Course:

The patient presented to the hospital with complaints of chest pain. Further evaluation revealed anterolateral STEMI for which the patient underwent percutaneous coronary intervention of the left circumflex. A chronic total occlusion of the left anterior descending was also noted. A transthoracic echocardiogram showed an ejection fraction of 10%-15% with dyskinetic apex, akinetic septum, mid to apical anterior, and lateral walls. An echodensity measuring 38 × 18 mm at its greatest dimension suggestive of a thrombus was also observed. The patient was discharged with Aspirin, Clopidogrel, and Rivaroxaban (15 mg daily for 3 weeks then 20 mg daily). A TTE performed three months later revealed improvement in the previously seen LVT with EF increasing to 35%.

Disposition:

The patient was discharged from the hospital in a stable condition with instructions on appropriate cardiac rehabilitation and follow-up. The patient was advised to continue with the prescribed medication regimen and to return to the clinic for further evaluation and monitoring as directed by his physicians.

Impression:

The patient presented with anterolateral STEMI requiring PCI of the left circumflex. Follow-up TTE revealed resolution of previously observed LVT with improvement in EF to 35%.

Write your reasoning in at most three short sentences, then a final line of exactly 'CODE: <letter><digit><digit>'.

text:
Anterolateral STEMI treated with PCI is the condition chiefly responsible for the admission; the LV thrombus is a complication of it. It is an acute myocardial infarction, in chapter I. The category is I21.

CODE: I21
